testName: Class A Knowledge Test #2 50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: What does an application pressure gauge show?

options.text: How much air pressure is being applied to the brakes.
How much air pressure is available.
How much air pressure is needed to stop a vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: How much air pressure is being applied to the brakes.
questions.explanation: An application pressure gauge shows how much air pressure is being applied to the brakes. This helps drivers know if their brakes are starting to fade.

questions.question: How can you stop a skid caused by over-acceleration?

options.text: Remove your foot from the accelerator.

questions.correctAnswerText: Remove your foot from the accelerator.
questions.explanation: Remove your foot from the accelerator to stop a skid caused by over-acceleration. This type of skid happens most often on snow or ice.

questions.question: What is the only way to become sober after drinking alcohol?
questions.explanation: The liver removes alcohol from your body at a fixed rate. Cold showers and black coffee will not speed this up. You must wait for your body to process the alcohol naturally.

questions.question: When driving at night, which of these should you NOT do?

options.text: Make sure your glasses are clean.

questions.explanation: Do not wear sunglasses when driving at night. If you wear glasses, keep them clean and scratch-free. Make sure you are rested and alert before driving at night.

questions.question: During a pre-trip inspection, what should you do with belts?

options.text: Leave them alone and do not inspect them.

questions.explanation: Check all belts for tightness and wear. Learn how much slack is normal for each belt.

questions.question: In cool weather, when ice begins to melt, what happens to the road?

options.text: It becomes safe to drive on.

questions.explanation: When ice melts, water sits on top of the remaining ice, making the road more slippery. Always slow down and drive carefully on slippery surfaces.

questions.question: When do you need an air brake endorsement?

options.text: To operate a vehicle with air brakes.
To drive any truck with a trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: To operate a vehicle with air brakes.
questions.explanation: You must pass an air brakes knowledge test to get a license to operate a vehicle with air brakes, including air over hydraulic braking systems.

questions.question: What is true about driving dry bulk tanks?

options.text: They cannot be driven on interstates.
They require special care to drive.
They are usually not allowed to cross railroad tracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: They require special care to drive.
questions.explanation: Dry bulk tanks need special care because they have high centers of gravity and the load can shift while moving.

questions.question: What is aggressive driving?

options.text: Operating a vehicle in a selfish or pushy manner.
Operating a vehicle with care for other drivers' safety.
Operating a vehicle in the left lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Operating a vehicle in a selfish or pushy manner.
questions.explanation: Aggressive driving is operating a vehicle in a selfish or pushy manner without regard for other drivers' rights or safety.

questions.question: What is a risk of cargo with a high center of gravity?

options.text: It can make a vehicle tip over.
It is encouraged in bad weather.
It is required on some roads.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can make a vehicle tip over.
questions.explanation: Cargo with a high center of gravity makes a vehicle more likely to tip. Keep cargo weight as low as possible.

questions.question: How can you avoid distracted driving?
questions.explanation: Distractions while driving can be physical (like reaching for objects), mental (like talking to passengers), or both (like texting on a phone). To avoid distracted driving: pre-program radio stations, plan your route ahead of time, avoid difficult conversations, adjust mirrors before driving, and do not eat, drink, or smoke while driving.

questions.question: What is removed when an air tank is drained?
questions.explanation: Air brake systems have drains to remove water and compressor oil that build up in the tanks. Water and oil in the system can damage the brakes.

questions.question: Eating while driving is:

options.text: A good way to save time.
Acceptable if you eat easy foods.

questions.explanation: Smoking, eating, and drinking are distracting activities and should not be done while driving. Plan ahead and stop to eat during long trips.

questions.question: If there is a fire in your vehicle, you should not:

options.text: Park in an open area away from buildings, trees, brush, and other vehicles.
Call emergency services with your location.

questions.explanation: If your vehicle catches fire, leave the road and stop in an open area. Do not go to a service station because fuel there could catch fire. Report the fire and your location to emergency services right away.

questions.question: What should you do before transporting an over-length load?

options.text: Alert fire departments along the route.

questions.explanation: Over-length, over-width, and overweight loads require special permits from the Department of Transportation.

questions.question: If you stay in neutral too long while switching gears:

options.text: You may have trouble putting the vehicle in the next gear.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may have trouble putting the vehicle in the next gear.
questions.explanation: Staying in neutral too long while switching gears can make it hard to shift into the next gear. If this happens, do not force the gear shift. Instead, go back to neutral, release the clutch, increase engine speed to match the road speed, and try again.

questions.question: When exiting a bus, a driver must:
questions.explanation: When exiting your vehicle during the basic vehicle control skills test, face the vehicle and keep three points of contact at all times. If your test vehicle is a bus, keep holding the handrail. Exiting incorrectly may result in automatic failure of the basic vehicle control skills test.

questions.question: Which is not a reason to cover cargo?

options.text: To protect people from spilled cargo

questions.explanation: Cover your cargo to protect people if cargo spills and to protect cargo from weather.

questions.question: During the vehicle inspection test, you will be asked to:

options.text: Explain what you inspect and why.

questions.correctAnswerText: Explain what you inspect and why.
questions.explanation: During the vehicle inspection test, you must do a complete inspection of your vehicle. You must explain to the examiner what you are inspecting and why.

questions.question: When should you adjust your mirrors?
questions.explanation: Check and adjust your mirrors before you start any trip.

questions.question: Are rims with welding repairs safe to use?

options.text: Yes, they are safe to use on rear tires.
Yes, they are safe if you are carrying a light load.

questions.explanation: Rims with welding repairs are never safe to use.

questions.question: What happens if brakes get too hot?
questions.explanation: Brakes can overheat and lose power. Do not rely only on brakes to slow your vehicle. Use engine braking to help slow down.

questions.question: What should you check on a belt-driven air compressor?
questions.explanation: Check the air compressor belt before each trip. Make sure it is tight and in good condition.

questions.question: What should you check on power steering hoses?

options.text: For the right amount of brake fluid.
To make sure they connect to the battery.

questions.explanation: When checking power steering, look at the hoses, pumps, and fluid level. Check the hoses for any leaks.

questions.question: Is texting while driving allowed?

options.text: Yes, if you are texting your employer.

questions.explanation: Texting while driving is dangerous and never allowed.

questions.question: When does hydroplaning happen most often?

options.text: When tire pressure is too low.
When tire tread is too deep.

questions.correctAnswerText: When tire pressure is too low.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when driving on wet roads with low tire pressure and worn tread. It can happen at speeds as low as 30 mph.

questions.question: Why should you do pre-trip inspections in the same order each time?

options.text: You will not forget any steps.

questions.correctAnswerText: You will not forget any steps.
questions.explanation: Using the same order each time helps you learn the steps and remember to check everything.

questions.question: What should you do if your vehicle hydroplanes?
questions.explanation: If your vehicle hydroplanes, do not brake. Release the accelerator and push in the clutch to slow down and regain traction.

questions.question: What should you do if an aggressive driver confronts you?

options.text: Keep your vehicle in front of them.

questions.explanation: Do not let their actions or angry gestures provoke you. Do not make eye contact. Get out of their way safely if you can.

questions.question: What should you do with your vehicle's gauges while driving?

options.text: Watch them for signs of trouble.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch them for signs of trouble.
questions.explanation: Watch your vehicle's gauges while driving for signs of problems. Check them before you start your trip to make sure they work properly.

questions.question: Loading weight high up on a vehicle:

options.text: Makes the vehicle more likely to tip over.
Makes items more likely to fall down.
Makes it harder to unload the cargo.

questions.correctAnswerText: Makes the vehicle more likely to tip over.
questions.explanation: Cargo loaded with a high center of gravity increases the risk that the vehicle will tip over. Load cargo evenly and keep weight low.

questions.question: Heights posted at bridges:
questions.explanation: Do not assume posted bridge heights are correct. Roads can change over time, such as from repaving or snow buildup, which affects clearance.

questions.question: Roads are most slippery right after rain starts because:

options.text: Water mixes with oil and grease on the road that haven't washed away yet.
Gravel gets washed to the middle of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Water mixes with oil and grease on the road that haven't washed away yet.
questions.explanation: Roads are very slippery when rain first starts. Water mixes with oil drippings on the road, creating a dangerous, slippery surface.

questions.question: What is the average driver's reaction time?
questions.explanation: The average driver's reaction time is between 3/4 of a second and one second. At 55 mph, you travel about 61 feet during this time.

questions.question: A ____ lets a driver apply spring brakes slowly.
questions.explanation: A modulating control valve lets a driver apply spring brakes gradually. It is controlled by a lever on the dashboard.

questions.question: Black ice is:
questions.explanation: Black ice is a thin, clear layer of ice. You can see the road through it, so it looks like a wet road. Watch for black ice when it looks wet but the temperature is below freezing.

questions.question: During the vehicle inspection test, you will:

options.text: Tell the examiner what you are checking and why.
Guess the weight of a load on a trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tell the examiner what you are checking and why.
questions.explanation: During the vehicle inspection test, you must inspect your entire vehicle. Tell the examiner what you are checking and explain why it matters.

questions.question: When turning, you should:

options.text: Turn off your signal just before turning.
Signal only if vehicles are ahead of you.

questions.explanation: Turn on your signal well before turning or changing lanes. Keep it on during the turn and turn it off after the turn is complete.

questions.question: When changing lanes, your turn signal:

options.text: Should only be used if traffic is present.
Should only be used between dusk and dawn.

questions.explanation: Always signal before turning or changing lanes, no matter what.

questions.question: Oversized loads:

options.text: Can never be transported by truck.
Should only be transported during daytime.
Need proper permits to follow state and local laws.

questions.correctAnswerText: Need proper permits to follow state and local laws.
questions.explanation: Special permits are required for loads that are oversized, overlong, or overweight.

questions.question: Vehicles with Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS) have ____ warning lamps that show when the ABS is not working.
questions.explanation: Vehicles with ABS have yellow warning lamps to alert drivers when the braking system is not working. Know where your vehicle's warning lamp is located before you drive.

questions.question: You should not use your mirrors to:

options.text: Determine how fast you are traveling.

questions.correctAnswerText: Determine how fast you are traveling.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors regularly, especially when changing lanes, turning, merging, and making tight maneuvers. However, do not use mirrors to check your speed.

questions.question: Your mirrors should be:

options.text: Checked only if you suspect a problem.

questions.explanation: Check your mirrors regularly while driving to stay aware of traffic and to check for problems with your vehicle.

questions.question: If you notice a safety problem or possible mechanical issue while driving, you should:

options.text: Wait to see if it goes away.
Write it down in your report.

questions.correctAnswerText: Write it down in your report.
questions.explanation: At the end of the day, you may need to fill out a written report on your vehicle's condition. Report anything that could affect safety or cause mechanical problems.

questions.question: When starting from a complete stop:

options.text: The vehicle should shift to the right.
The vehicle should be in third gear.
The vehicle should not roll backward.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle should not roll backward.
questions.explanation: Make sure your vehicle does not roll backward when you start from a complete stop. This prevents hitting anything behind you.

questions.question: When you start your vehicle, the coolant temperature should:

options.text: Jump quickly from low to high.

questions.explanation: Check your gauges before you drive. After starting the engine, the coolant temperature should increase slowly until it reaches normal operating temperature.

questions.question: Load blocking:

options.text: Is dangerous and should never be done.
Keeps cargo from shifting during transport.
Is only used for liquid cargo.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keeps cargo from shifting during transport.
questions.explanation: Blocking and bracing prevent cargo from moving while the vehicle is being transported.

questions.question: The center of gravity in a trailer should be:

options.text: At the rear of the trailer.

questions.explanation: Place cargo as low as possible in the vehicle. A center of gravity that is too high increases the risk of a rollover.

questions.question: If your vehicle is hydroplaning, you should:
questions.explanation: If your vehicle begins to hydroplane, do not brake. Instead, release the accelerator and push in the clutch to slow down.

questions.question: Air brakes use ____ to work.
questions.explanation: Air brake systems use compressed air to operate the brakes.
